author: Dan Abrams
text:
When a bead exceeds stuck_bead_threshold, it's skipped but never closed or deprioritized. beads.Ready() returns the same stuck bead on the next iteration, creating an infinite loop of 'Skipped after N failures' logs with duplicate comments added each time. Loops until maxIterations.

Fix: After skipping a stuck bead, call beads.ReadyAny() or track skipped IDs in a set to get the NEXT bead instead. If all beads are stuck, exit the loop cleanly with a message.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stuck beads are skipped exactly once per run, not re-fetched
- If all ready beads are stuck, loop exits with clear message
- No duplicate comments added to stuck beads

Key files: internal/runner/runner.go (lines 168-179)

author: Dan Abrams
text:
Three different JSON extraction strategies exist:
1. ParseScopeEstimate (prompt.go) -- first '{' to last '}'
2. parseAnalysisOutput (analyzer.go) -- same first/last bracket approach
3. ParseProposals (proposals.go) -- regex for fenced code blocks
4. parseDecomposeOutput (runner.go) -- raw Unmarshal, no extraction

Create a shared utility (e.g. internal/llmjson/extract.go) that tries:
1. Extract from fenced code block (most robust)
2. Fall back to bracket matching
3. Fall back to raw unmarshal

Then use it in all four call sites.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single ExtractJSON(output string, target any) function
- Used by all four parsers
- Tests cover: pure JSON, code-fenced JSON, JSON with surrounding text, arrays and objects
- Existing tests still pass

Key files: internal/prompt/prompt.go, internal/analyzer/analyzer.go, internal/retro/proposals.go, internal/runner/runner.go

author: Dan Abrams
text:
The core loop (processBead, retry/escalation, stuck bead skipping, decomposition) has zero test coverage. TestRetryCounterBehavior is a no-op.

Depends on: ralph-runner-thd (interfaces for testability)

Write integration tests using mock dependencies:
1. Happy path: bead fetched, claude succeeds, validation passes, bead closed
2. Retry path: claude fails, retried on same model, succeeds
3. Escalation path: claude fails, escalates haiku->sonnet->opus
4. Stuck bead path: bead exceeds threshold, skipped
5. Decomposition path: all models exhausted, decompose triggers

Also: delete TestRetryCounterBehavior (the no-op documentary test).

Acceptance criteria:
- 5 integration tests covering the above scenarios
- TestRetryCounterBehavior removed
- Tests use mock interfaces, not real CLI

Key files: internal/runner/runner_test.go

author: Dan Abrams
text:
parseDecomposeOutput (runner.go:1082) does raw json.Unmarshal on Claude's full output, expecting pure JSON with no surrounding text. Unlike ParseScopeEstimate (which finds {/}) and ParseProposals (which extracts from code blocks), this breaks if Claude adds any preamble or wraps in a code fence.

Fix: Extract JSON array from output using bracket matching (find first '[' and last ']'), similar to how ParseScopeEstimate works for objects. Consider also extracting from code blocks as a first attempt.

Acceptance criteria:
- Parsing succeeds when Claude wraps array in a code block
- Parsing succeeds when Claude adds text before/after the JSON
- Parsing still works for pure JSON output
- Add test cases for all three scenarios

Key files: internal/runner/runner.go (parseDecomposeOutput, line 1082)

text:
When running with --time-budget, light reviews and thorough reviews don't check the deadline. A review triggered near the budget boundary could run well past the intended cutoff. The review invocations in runner.go should check the run deadline before starting and either skip the review or use a reduced timeout.

Key files: internal/runner/runner.go

author: Dan Abrams
text:
Three issues with ralph init output:

1. defaultRetroTemplate in init.go uses old markdown output format, not the structured JSON format that ParseProposals() expects. New projects always fall back to non-interactive mode.

2. init.go doesn't create PROMPT_scope.md or PROMPT_decompose.md. If scope check or decomposition triggers, it fails with 'no such file or directory'.

3. Default config in init.go is missing scope_check section, max_retries_per_bead, bead_timeout, stall_timeout_active, analysis_timeout.

Acceptance criteria:
- defaultRetroTemplate matches current .ralph/templates/PROMPT_retro.md (structured JSON output)
- init creates PROMPT_scope.md and PROMPT_decompose.md
- Default config includes scope_check section and missing tuning knobs

Key files: cmd/ralph/init.go, .ralph/templates/PROMPT_retro.md, .ralph/templates/PROMPT_scope.md, .ralph/templates/PROMPT_decompose.md

- Validation config respects Enabled as precedent (see runner.go:631)

text:
Closed: This bead violates the '2-file maximum' rule by touching interface definitions, multiple mock implementations, and potentially many callers. Decomposing into:

1. gromit-tabl-1: Add ReadyWithLabel/ListWithLabel signatures to BeadClient interface (internal/runner/interfaces.go only)
2. gromit-tabl-2: Update test mocks in internal/runner to implement new interface methods
3. gromit-tabl-3: Update any other callers/mocks to satisfy the new interface

See LEARNINGS.md: interface changes are cross-cutting and should be split by concern (definition, mock implementation, callers).

author: Dan Abrams
text:
runner.go depends on concrete types (*bead.Client, *claude.Client, *analyzer.Analyzer, *prompt.Renderer, *logger.Logger) with no interface abstractions. The core loop is untestable without real CLI processes.

Define interfaces at the point of use in runner.go:
- beadClient interface { Ready() (*bead.Bead, error); Close(id string) error; ... }
- claudeRunner interface { Run(ctx, prompt, model string) (*claude.Result, error); ... }
- Keep interfaces minimal -- only the methods runner actually calls

Then update NewRunner to accept interfaces. This unblocks integration tests for processBead.

Acceptance criteria:
- Interfaces defined for bead, claude, and analyzer dependencies
- Runner uses interfaces instead of concrete types
- A mock implementation exists for each interface (in runner_test.go)
- All existing tests still pass

Key files: internal/runner/runner.go
